newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks end higher, helped by blue-chips.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks end higher, helped by blue-chips.

text.p: ** (1330 GMT) - Indian blue chips in late rally, end with
modest gains helped by investment buying
** Bombay share index rallies 36.10 points, or 0.86
percent, to end at 4,217.58, near day's highs
** Shares of Industrial Credit & Investment Corporation of
India jump 10 pct as investors bid in the stock after
firm posts sharp rise in 1997/98 first quarter net
** Supreme Court dismisses bail plea of former Bihar chief
minister Laloo Prasad Yadav seeking legal protection
** National exchange index up 8.65 pts at 1,190.30, Delhi
6.25 pts at 882.45 and Madras 16.42 pts at 4,295.95
Indian bourses closed with modest gains on Tuesday, piggy-backing on a late surge in blue chip stocks, dealers said.

"Typically, some form of consolidation is good for the market," said Kuntal Shah, chief dealer at brokerage D.T. Gandhi. "It appears that speculators are losing interest in top stocks and diverting funds to smaller, second-liner shares."
Many participants were awaiting a clear market trend and were keen buyers only in individual stocks which had positive fundamentals, traders said.

Shares of Industrial Credit & Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) topped the list of winners on Tuesday, surging 10 percent as foreign funds bid in the stock after the firm posted a sharp rise in first-quarter net profit.
ICICI rose 8.75 rupees to close at 97.0, a new 52-week high, in heavy volume of 2.67 million shares compared with Monday's volume of 934,189 shares.
The term-lending institution on Monday announced a net profit of 2.23 billion rupees in the three months to June 30 against 1.0 billion rupees in the same period a year earlier.
The results were released shortly after market hours.
"The company showed a very good performance," said Govind Agarwal, institutional sales dealer at Motilal Oswal Securities.
The market had largely discounted the possibility of Laloo Prasad Yadav, former Bihar chief minister, being arrested after the Supreme Court on Tuesday dismissed a bail plea of Yadav.
Yadav was forced to resign last week Friday after a special court issued arrest warrants against him and three other politicians in a $280-million corruption scandal.
The National Stock Exchange said it had advanced trading hours by 30 minutes from Wednesday.Under the new timing, trading will start at 0930 local (0300 GMT) and end at 1500 (0930 GMT).
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
